updates: Draggy now runs on the same Tauri app on Windows, macOS and Linux, with one look, shell and setup everywhere.
macOS is back as one universal app for Apple silicon and Intel Macs running macOS 14 or newer. It is signed ad hoc, so clear the quarantine flag or use right click, Open the first time.
Linux gets an AppImage next to the .deb and .rpm packages.
Every platform now updates itself from its own signed feed. Windows users on build 16 need to install build 17 by hand once; later builds arrive on their own.
Video tools on macOS and Linux use a bundled ffmpeg, so you no longer need to install one.
API server settings are easier to read and set up.
Models from an added provider now have an on/off switch and start switched on.
Draggy reads the context window from llama.cpp and vLLM model lists.
fixes: Adding a Custom (OpenAI-compatible) provider works again.
Free disk space shows the right number on macOS.
Chat stays visible when you drag the side pane wide.
Web searches no longer come back empty when a search engine shows a bot check.

updates: macOS builds are paused for now. This build ships for Windows and Linux only, and macOS will come back in a later build.
Download errors now tell you what to do about a full disk, a folder you can't write to, a bad checksum or a blocked address.
Skills switched on past the 40th can still be used.
fixes: Model downloads on Windows no longer fail with "URL refused by outbound security policy".
Closing or crashing Draggy no longer leaves llama-server or shell processes running.
MCP tools that only claim to be read-only now ask before they run, and web fetches stop at 16 MiB.
When several files change at once, every one of them is picked up, so open canvases no longer go stale.
Enter with an input method editor, Escape in menus and rename, and retry on the crash screen work again.
AI could not read videos because of "Disabled tools" but now can.
